claim: TikTok's own newsroom post pins the exact effective-date sequence of its monetization overhaul: Creativity Program Beta launched invite-only 20 February 2023 (US, France, Brazil); opened to all eligible US creators (10,000+ followers, 100,000+ authentic video views in 30 days) on 3 May 2023; and fully replaced the Creator Fund in the US, UK, France and Germany on 16 December 2023.
stance_target: platform monetization-scheme changes have precisely datable effective dates that break year-over-year income comparability
scope_conditions: Platform-disclosed, dated by TikTok itself via in-place update notices on the same post; the four named markets (US, UK, France, Germany) are the only ones confirmed by this source for the 16 Dec 2023 full-replacement date -- rollout timing for other countries, including Southeast Asian markets, is not disclosed here
quoted_support: [UPDATE - November 6, 2023]: Starting December 16, 2023, the Creativity Program will fully replace the Creator Fund in the US, UK, France, and Germany. ... [UPDATE - May 3, 2023]: Beginning May 3, 2023, US creators with at least 10K followers and 100K authentic video views in the last 30 days are eligible to join the Creativity Program Beta.
region: US, UK, France, Germany (confirmed); Brazil (beta only)

claim: The Creativity Program introduced a structural eligibility change beyond just payout rate: to earn, creators must publish original content longer than one minute, whereas the legacy Creator Fund paid on videos of any length -- meaning the payout-rate shift is confounded with a content-format eligibility shift, not a clean like-for-like rate change.
stance_target: the pre/post monetization-program cohorts are not directly comparable even setting aside the RPM change, because the underlying content eligible for monetization changed too
scope_conditions: US-focused announcement; does not specify whether this content-length rule applied identically upon the 16 Dec 2023 full replacement in UK/France/Germany
quoted_support: To start earning, creators must create and publish high-quality, original content longer than one minute.
